A Letter, Sealed for Her

❖
To My Little Sis, Mina ❤️

Happy 18th birthday, you idiot. ❤️

Eighteen.

It feels strange even writing that.

Somehow, through all the chaos, all the late-night conversations, stupid jokes, random arguments, countless VCs, games, laughter, silence, and everything in between, we've made it here. Almost two years of knowing you, watching you grow, watching you change, watching you figure yourself out little by little—and now you're finally eighteen.

An adult.

Although, honestly, I don't think that means you're suddenly allowed to stop being my little sis. 😂

When I look back at everything we've been through, I'm genuinely proud of you. Not just because of the things you've achieved, but because I've seen you during the moments when things weren't going well too. I've seen your highs, your lows, your excitement, your frustration, your happiness, your sadness, your moments where you felt completely lost, and the moments where you somehow found your way again.

And through all of that, somehow, we stayed.

We've had periods where we talked for hours and hours, where we could sit in VC doing absolutely nothing and still somehow have the best time. We've had periods where life got busy, where things became quiet, where we weren't around each other as much. And even now, while I'm writing this, we're going through one of those quieter phases.

But even in the silence, one thing hasn't changed for me.

You're still my best friend.

You're still my little sis.

And you're still someone I'm incredibly proud to have in my life.

I don't think people always realize how much they can change someone else's life simply by being there. You've done that for me in ways you probably don't even know. There are moments I remember not because something extraordinary happened, but because you were there. A random conversation. A stupid joke. A late-night VC. A game we played. A moment where one of us was having a terrible day and somehow the other made it a little lighter.

Those little things stay.

And that's what I hope you remember too.

As you step into eighteen, you're going to experience so many new things. You're going to grow, change, make mistakes, fall in love with things, lose interest in others, meet people, lose people, discover parts of yourself you didn't know existed, and probably make some absolutely questionable decisions along the way. 😂

And that's okay.

You don't have to have your entire life figured out just because you've turned eighteen.

You don't have to become some perfect version of yourself overnight.

You just have to keep moving.

Keep learning.

Keep becoming the person you want to be.

And whenever life becomes heavy, I hope you remember that you've already made it through every difficult day you've faced so far. Every bad day eventually became a day you survived. Every difficult phase eventually became a chapter you could look back on.

So don't be afraid of the chapters ahead.

Write them.

Mess them up.

Rewrite them. Make them yours.

And wherever life takes you, I hope you never lose the parts of yourself that make you you.

The person who gets excited over the smallest things.

The person who can be unbelievably stubborn.

The person who can disappear into her own world.

The person who can care so deeply even when she doesn't always know how to show it.

The person who somehow manages to make life more chaotic and more memorable at the same time.

That's the Mina I've known.

That's the Mina I've watched grow.

And that's the Mina I'm proud of.

I'm proud of you, little sis.

I'm proud that I got to be your friend through these years.

I'm proud of all the things you've accomplished.

I'm proud of the person you're becoming.

And more than anything, I'm grateful that somewhere along the way, two people met and somehow ended up becoming family in their own weird little way.

Two years later, here we are.

And who knows what the next two years will look like?

Maybe we'll talk every day.

Maybe we'll disappear into our own lives for months at a time.

Maybe we'll argue over something incredibly stupid.

Maybe we'll sit in VC for six hours again doing absolutely nothing.

Maybe we'll look back at this letter years from now and laugh at how dramatic I was writing it. 😂

Whatever happens, I hope you know that the time we've already shared mattered to me.

You mattered to me.

You still do.

So here's to eighteen. Here's to growing up without losing yourself. Here's to becoming stronger without becoming colder. Here's to finding happiness without having to chase it. Here's to all the things you haven't experienced yet. And here's to every version of you that you'll become along the way.

Happy 18th birthday, Mina.

Keep your head up.

Keep your heart soft.

Keep being you.

And remember that somewhere out there is your annoying older-brother-best-friend who is genuinely, ridiculously proud of you.

Happy birthday, little sis. ❤️

— Your homie, Nigel 🐾
